summary: Iteration 3 (light theme + batch traceability workflow) tested end-to-end. Backend: 18/18 pytest cases pass covering telemetry, migrated statuses (PLANNED/PROCESSING/PAUSED/COMPLETED), auth-gated create/status/events endpoints, invalid-status 400, missing-batch 404, full workflow (create PLANNED → PROCESSING → PAUSED → RESUME → custom event → COMPLETED with final_weight_kg → 24-point temp/weight histories + LPG/electrical energy + QR Issued), persistence via GET, and energy/summary + system/status. Found and fixed one CRITICAL backend bug introduced by the status rename (see rca). Frontend: end-to-end UI workflow driven by Playwright — login → New Batch form (all 9 new testids present, batch-id readOnly + auto-generated) → submit shows batch-created-card → Open Batch Record → Batch Detail /batches/:id renders traceability-timeline + all sections + no-history-note in PLANNED → Start Processing → Pause → Resume → record custom event via event-form → Complete with final_weight 14.5 kg → status COMPLETED, temp-history-chart + weight-history-chart + view-passport-link visible, output shows 14.5 kg / 29.0% yield, energy shows 0.09 kg LPG / 0.01 kWh, event-form hidden → reload persists all data → Batch History shows new batch with Open link + PROCESSING/COMPLETED badges → Dashboard shows subtle amber SIMULATED / DEMO banner → Energy analytics page loads (previously 500) → Logout returns to /login. Light theme verified via computed body background rgb(244,246,248).

minor.issue: (FIXED) Was querying db.batches by status='COMPLETE' after the status rename, resulting in empty list → ZeroDivisionError → HTTP 500. Renamed to 'COMPLETED'.
(carried over from iter 2) brute-force lockout keyed only on email now — acceptable but exposes admin to lockout DoS by attacker knowing the email. Consider IP+email with real X-Forwarded-For.

issues: Recharts logs width(-1)/height(-1) warnings on initial mount because the two chart containers use h-48 inside a lg:grid-cols-2 wrapper whose columns start at 0 width during layout thrash. Non-blocking (charts render correctly after layout settles) but pollutes console. Suggest wrapping ResponsiveContainer with a min-width:0 grid child, e.g. add min-w-0 to the wrapping div.

action_items: (Optional polish) Add min-w-0 to the two chart-column divs in /app/frontend/src/pages/BatchDetail.jsx to silence recharts width(-1) warnings on completion.
(Security, deferred from iter 2) Consider hardening brute-force lockout key using X-Forwarded-For, not client host.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py had a stale 'COMPLETE' literal in energy_summary after renaming statuses to COMPLETED — always grep-audit legacy strings when renaming enums. Fixed in this iteration.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup') / 'shutdown') — migrate to FastAPI lifespan context manager (flagged in iterations 1 and 2, still open).
server.py status migration runs on every startup via update_many({status: RUNNING/COMPLETE}) — idempotent, OK, but consider one-off migration script.

BatchDetail.jsx recomputes gridStatus/solarStatus/batteryStatus from substring of electrical_source string — brittle; would break if the option label changes. Consider structured energy-source config.

NewBatch.jsx auto-batch-id computed from client-side max is racy (two operators could get the same suggested id, server dedupes to 409). Acceptable for demo; server-side generation on create is the true source of truth.

rca of the issue: GET /api/energy/summary returned HTTP 500 after this iteration migrated batch statuses from COMPLETE→COMPLETED. Root cause: the query filter in energy_summary() was not updated with the rest of the codebase and still filtered by {'status':'COMPLETE'}, returning zero completed batches. Downstream f-string 'round(total_hours / len(completed), 1)' then divided by 0 → ZeroDivisionError. Reproduction: curl /api/energy/summary → 500 (traceback in supervisor backend.err.log). Mitigation applied: renamed the filter to 'COMPLETED' in /app/backend/server.py line 424. Verified: endpoint now returns 200 with batches_completed>=1. Prevention: introduce a BatchStatus enum shared between server and frontend, and grep-audit all string literals when renaming.
